prompt: Edit the FIRST image. It is an animator's layout sheet: 3 posing mannequins in a 3x1 grid, 3 key drawing(s) of him for one film shot: Tane, the delinquent, comes bursting through a shut steel shutter shoulder first (drawing 1: in the air, left shoulder and left knee leading, right arm flung wide, coat flaring, a huge fearless grin, eyes on the viewer); lands in a wide low skid on his wooden sandals (drawing 2: braced, arms out, coat swinging, grinning, head turned to look back the way he came, toward the RIGHT of the picture); and stands up out of it (drawing 3: a fist on his hip, glancing back over his shoulder toward the RIGHT of the picture with a cocky grin, pupils in the corners of his eyes) (reading left to right). Paint the character from the SECOND image (his model sheet) over every mannequin, as 3 finished key drawings by the same animator. The second image only shows what he looks like: do not copy its standing figures, its poses or its arrangement; the result holds exactly the 3 figures of the first image, each in its mannequin's pose and place, and nothing else. For each of the 3: keep every limb exactly where the mannequin has it (same joint positions and angles, same lean, same head position, same size and same place in its cell), so the 3 figures stay the same size as each other. BLUE limbs are his LEFT arm and leg; RED limbs are his RIGHT arm and leg; the darker shade is the upper limb, the lighter the lower. Each mannequin is drawn in the exact PERSPECTIVE of the film camera of its shot, and the drawing must keep that camera: drawing 1 is seen in three-quarter FRONT view, his LEFT side nearer the viewer, at about eye level; drawing 2 is seen from straight in front, at about eye level; drawing 3 is seen from straight in front, at about eye level. Keep each mannequin's foreshortening exactly: what is nearer the camera is drawn bigger, what points away from it is drawn shorter, and the figure's outline matches its mannequin's outline. Do NOT turn the figure to a plainer view. Each figure has exactly two arms and two legs, and both feet are drawn complete. Wherever his face shows it is fully drawn, with eyes, eyebrows, nose and mouth as on the model sheet: never a blank face. All 3 drawings must be the SAME character with IDENTICAL design, colours and details in every drawing: Tane, a 16-year-old boy, stocky and a bit fat with a soft round belly, warm medium-brown skin and thick eyebrows. HAIR: a tall glossy black pompadour swept up and forward, short at the sides and back. COAT: a long plain dark-red coat down to his calves, always worn open, with a high stand-up collar and long sleeves to the wrists; four round gold buttons in a row down the front edge on HIS RIGHT side and nothing else on it; the back of the coat is plain dark red with one centre seam. BELLY WRAP: a white sleeveless undershirt tucked into a wide white cloth wrap wound round his whole belly from chest to waist, drawn with three or four horizontal fold lines. TROUSERS: plain baggy black trousers gathered at the ankles. FEET: bare feet in wooden geta sandals: a plain light-brown wooden block sole with one black V-shaped strap between the toes. HANDS: bare hands, no gloves, no rings. FACE: round cheeks, thick black eyebrows, a wide fearless grin showing his teeth. No pins, no badges, no emblems, no insignia, no stars, no lettering, no numbers, no logos and no brand marks anywhere on him. No toothpick, no cigarette, no weapon. Remove every trace of the mannequins: no blue, red, green or grey mannequin colour may remain. Style as the second image: 1990s cel anime: bold clean black ink outlines of even weight, flat colour fills, two tones per material (a base and one hard-edged shade), no gradients, no texture, no soft shading, no motion blur, no speed lines, no ground, no shadows on the ground, no text, no panel borders. Background: one flat solid pure magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, also between the legs and inside every gap. In all three drawings his FACE is toward the viewer and fully drawn (the mannequin's pale head block is his pompadour, which sweeps up and forward above his forehead; his face is below it). No toothpick, no stick in his mouth, no earring, no pipe, nothing in his hands: his fists are empty. The coat's buttons and every other detail are on the same side as on the model sheet.
